newsitem.title: JAPAN: Economists expect small Japan supplementary budget.
newsitem.headline: Economists expect small Japan supplementary budget.

text.p: Japan is likely to draft a supplementary national budget this fiscal year in a bid to help the economy remain on track.
But as a stimulative step, it is expected to be much smaller than past efforts and may be later than first thought, economists said on Thursday.

Most domestic research houses have put the size of the budget at somewhere between two trillion and three trillion yen, although some foreign houses have forecast it at between four trillion and six trillion yen.
This is much smaller than last September's massive 14 trillion yen stimulus package of mainly public works spending.
To finance part of that spending, the government adopted a five trillion yen supplementary budget in October.
The government has said it will make a decision on whether to form an extra budget after April-June gross domestic product (GDP) data is released later this month.
Economists said despite growing pressure for fiscal restraint, politicians will be reluctant to break completely with the years-long tradition of using extra public works spending to please voters.
"The political dynamic here is a still very expansionary one," said Russell Jones, chief economist at Lehman Brothers in Tokyo.
But many also said elections, if held early, could mean the extra budget may be postponed until the beginning of the year.
"They might decide to put it off. A budget announcement at the beginning of October is looking less likely," said Hisashi Yamada, an economist at Japan Research Ltd.
A Reuters Financial Television survey showed that five out of 10 analysts expect general elections this year.
A general election must be held before next July.
